causes.label: wind_output
causes.quote: Wind generation fell significantly in the lead up to 1 am, which reduced the amount of low-priced capacity available because wind is typically offered at negative prices.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: An unplanned outage on the Murraylink interconnector prevented imports from Victoria, further limiting South Australia's access to low-priced generation.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: These factors, combined with market participants rebidding roughly 135 MW of capacity to high prices, contributed to the 1 am 30-minute price exceeding $5,000/MWh.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: The remaining interconnector linking South Australia to Victoria, the Heywood interconnector, was operating at 544 MW at 12.30 am, close to its 600 MW nominal capacity. This meant South Australia could not import significantly more cheap capacity from Victoria when the price rose.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: At 12.40 am the price first exceeded $400/MWh and reached $4,093/MWh. Subsequently, fast-start' units received a signal to come on but required 10 to 15 minutes before they could begin generating. This meant that a high price was able to persist until 1 am, when these units could increase their generation.

interconnectors_named.name: Murraylink interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: An unplanned outage on the Murraylink interconnector prevented imports from Victoria, further limiting South Australia's access to low-priced generation.

interconnectors_named.name: Heywood interconnector
interconnectors_named.quote: The remaining interconnector linking South Australia to Victoria, the Heywood interconnector, was operating at 544 MW at 12.30 am, close to its 600 MW nominal capacity.

intervals.quote: The 30-minute price in South Australia was $5,715/MWh at 1 am on 18 December 2021. This was driven by two 5-minute prices of $10,247/MWh and $15,098/MWh at 12.50 am and 12.55 am respectively.
